articles.title: Travis Hunter sets the internet on fire with his dancing ability while catching footballs
articles.summary: Even though the Jacksonville Jaguars lost 34-17 to the Carolina Panthers in a 2026 Preseason Week 2 game at EverBank Stadium, Travis Hunter set the internet on fire with his dance moves while catching footballs.
articles.body:
Even though the Jacksonville Jaguars lost 34-17 to the Carolina Panthers in a 2026 Preseason Week 2 game at EverBank Stadium, Travis Hunter set the internet on fire with his dance moves while catching footballs.

The former Heisman Trophy winner didn’t get to play, but fans were loving the show he put on while being at the sidelines.

Despite the loss, there was a strong showing early for the Jaguars Friday: the play of rookie wide receivers CJ Williams and Josh Cameron, a pair of sixth-round '26 selections who have impressed throughout training camp and the preseason.

articles.title: Travis Hunter’s biggest allies in Jacksonville’s championship pursuit could be two wideout rookies
articles.standfirst: The newcomers have shown ability and speed that can give defenses nightmares
articles.summary: The newcomers have shown ability and speed that can give defenses nightmares
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars may have suffered a 34-17 preseason loss to the Carolina Panthers on Friday night, but the final score was not the most important takeaway from EverBank Stadium. Instead, some of the most encouraging developments came from two rookies who continue to build momentum heading toward the regular season.

Wide receivers CJ Williams and Josh Cameron , both selected in the sixth round of the 2026 NFL Draft , once again flashed the potential that has made them two of the most talked-about young players in J acksonville's training camp. And if their development continues, they could become valuable allies for superstar rookie Travis Hunter as the Jaguars attempt to build a roster capable of competing for a championship.

Hunter entered the NFL with enormous expectations. As one of the most dynamic prospects in recent memory, his ability to impact games in multiple ways has generated excitement throughout Jacksonville. But even generational talents need support, and the Jaguars may have found two unexpected contributors who can help lighten the load. Against Carolina, both Williams and Cameron continued their impressive preseason performances.

Depth often determines whether a season ends in January or February

Cameron hauled in two receptions for 41 yards during the first half, showcasing the big-play ability that has consistently appeared throughout camp. Williams , meanwhile, recorded four catches for 22 yards, continuing to demonstrate reliability and route-running precision. Neither performance will dominate national headlines, but inside the Jaguars' building, the contributions have not gone unnoticed.

Head coach Liam Coen offered strong praise for both rookies after the game, highlighting not only their on-field production but also the professional habits that have accelerated their development. That type of endorsement carries significant weight, especially for late-round draft picks fighting to establish themselves on an NFL roster.

For championship contenders, depth often determines whether a season ends in January or February. Teams that can consistently uncover contributors beyond the first few rounds of the draft gain a significant advantage, particularly when injuries inevitably test a roster's depth. The Jaguars appear hopeful that Williams and Cameron can become those kinds of players.

Defenses could find themselves facing difficult decisions

Both receivers have earned attention throughout training camp by consistently making plays, understanding the offensive system, and displaying maturity beyond their years. Their strong work ethic has translated into opportunities during preseason action, and they have capitalized on those chances.

That development could prove especially important for Hunter. As Jacksonville continues integrating its highly touted rookie into the offense, opposing defenses will inevitably devote considerable attention to slowing him down. The emergence of additional receiving threats would make that task far more difficult.

If Williams and Cameron continue progressing, defenses could find themselves facing difficult decisions. Focus too heavily on Hunter, and the rookie receivers may exploit favorable matchups. Shift attention elsewhere, and Travis could take over games with his unique playmaking ability. That is how dangerous offenses are built.

articles.title: Travis Hunter stunned as police make major drug bust during ride-along
articles.summary: Travis Hunter got an unexpected look at police work during a recent ride-along with Jacksonville Sheriff T.K. Waters, when officers showed the Jaguars star a bag of drugs allegedly recovered during a traffic stop.
articles.body:
Travis Hunter got an unexpected look at police work during a recent ride-along with Jacksonville Sheriff T.K. Waters, when officers showed the Jaguars star a bag of drugs allegedly recovered during a traffic stop.

The bust reportedly involved marijuana, meth, suspected cocaine and fentanyl, leaving Hunter stunned before he joked that police had caught a “kingpin” and warned kids to stay away from drugs.

The NFL star is preparing for his second season with the Jaguars after appearing in just seven games as a rookie, but after witnessing the dramatic bust firsthand, it seems he may have a future in law enforcement if football ever takes a back seat.

articles.title: Jacksonville Jaguars: Here’s how the new uniform pays tribute to the city
articles.standfirst: The Jaguars’ new design changes their look for the 2026 season.
articles.summary: The Jaguars’ new design changes their look for the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars have a new look for the 2026 season. The team, along with Nike and the NFL, unveiled its “Bold City Glow” rivalry uniform, a design that moves away from the franchise’s usual color combination in favor of a different aesthetic and, above all, one that is much more connected to Jacksonville.

The new uniform features a color that is different from the shade that typically defines the team: a cream color inspired by Florida’s coastal culture. It is paired with the word “Jaguars” in a cursive font and numbers that combine matte and glossy finishes . The outside of the collar also features the inscription “Since '95,” referring to the year the franchise was founded.

However, the most striking and significant change appears on the head. For the first time in franchise history, the Jaguars will wear a shiny teal helmet, complete with a gold face mask and the regional “904” mark.

But the changes and the connection to Jacksonville do not end there.

What is hidden in the Jaguars’ new uniform?

The pants feature a black base with a subtle jaguar-spot pattern, along with a teal stripe outlined in gold. However, the pattern hides a detail that directly connects the uniform to the city .

Hidden among the spots are the names of different Jacksonville neighborhoods, incorporated into the design as a tribute to the communities that are part of the city’s identity .

When will the Jaguars debut the new uniform?

Although the design has already been unveiled, fans will have to wait to see it in an official game. The Jaguars will debut the uniform in Week 8, on November 1, 2026, when they host the Indianapolis Colts, one of their division rivals .

Jacksonville finished the 2025 season with a 13-4 record, won the AFC South , and closed the regular season with eight consecutive victories. However, their run ended in the Wild Card Round with a 27-24 loss to the Buffalo Bills.

Now, the new uniform marks the beginning of another chapter for the franchise, but its meaning goes beyond the football field.

articles.title: Quinn Ewers fails to convince Dolphins and joins Jaguars alongside Travis Hunter for fresh start
articles.standfirst: Jacksonville has taken a chance on the former Texas quarterback after Miami decided to move on.
articles.summary: Jacksonville has taken a chance on the former Texas quarterback after Miami decided to move on.
articles.body:
Quinn Ewers is getting another opportunity to change the direction of his NFL career after the Miami Dolphins traded the former Texas star to the Jacksonville Jaguars .

Jacksonville sent Miami a sixth-round pick in the 2028 NFL Draft for Ewers , who now joins an offense featuring Trevor Lawrence and Travis Hunter .

The move comes after Ewers struggled to secure his place in Miami’s plans following an uneven preseason and a groin injury.

“Yeah, I think so. Quinn really hasn’t been able to go very much,” Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said when asked earlier in the week whether the backup quarterback competition was still open.

Dolphins move on from Quinn Ewers

Ewers had shown promise late in the 2025 season after replacing Tua Tagovailoa as Miami’s starter.

He appeared in four games and made three starts, completing 55 of 83 passes for 622 yards and three touchdowns.

But his 2026 preseason got off to a difficult start.

Ewers completed just one of eight passes for 27 yards and an interception against Washington before a groin injury prevented him from playing in Miami’s next two preseason games.

Reports subsequently suggested there were differing opinions inside the Dolphins organization over whether he should remain on the roster.

“There were mixed views internally about keeping him. There was sentiment in front office for a different no. 2,” Miami Herald reporter Barry Jackson wrote.

Jaguars give Ewers another opportunity

Jacksonville had been searching for more depth behind Lawrence and ultimately decided Ewers was worth the investment.

“The Jaguars have been quietly calling around on backup QBs and land one with Ewers, who has starting experience,” NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported.

Ewers now enters a quarterback room that also includes Nick Mullens, Carter Bradley and Joey Aguilar , although the trade could lead to further roster changes before the season begins.

His arrival also places him on the same roster as Hunter , giving Jacksonville another young player with significant college pedigree.

Ewers was originally selected 231st overall by Miami in the seventh round of the 2025 NFL Draft after leading Texas to consecutive College Football Playoff semifinal appearances.

Now, after only one season with the Dolphins , Jacksonville offers him a fresh chance to prove that his brief spell as an NFL starter wasn't the ceiling of his professional career.

articles.title: Trevor Lawrence's TSA Screening at airport alongside Liam Coen was somehow the key to Jaguars success
articles.standfirst: It goes to show that quarterback-coach relationships take time to cultivate.
articles.summary: It goes to show that quarterback-coach relationships take time to cultivate.
articles.body:
Heading into the 2025 season, after four years with the Jacksonville Jaguars , it would have been slightly harsh to call Trevor Lawrence a "bust". But given the elite ceiling he showed in college, the former No. 1 overall pick left fans wanting a lot more.

Midway through the 2025 season, it looked to be more of the same from Lawrence . Despite having an offensive guru in Liam Coen as his new head coach, Lawrence was still committing too many turnovers and taking too many sacks . Even after winning a second straight game and bringing the team's record to 7-4 , Lawrence had just thrown three interception against the Arizona Cardinals .

Thankfully, he also threw three touchdowns in that game, and averaged 8.5 yards per pass attempt . While the quarterback wasn't thrilled with his performance in that game, a huge vote of confidence from Coen ended up turning around Lawrence's season - and it happened during a TSA Screening process at the airport .

Liam Coen inspired confidence in Trevor Lawrence following three-touchdown, three-interception game

While speaking to Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer , Lawrence explained how his conversation with Coen in the TSA Screening Line fortified their relationship and set them on the right track.

That game, I really thought we started to click offensively. We had a lot of turnovers, but we did some really good things in the passing game. It was the most on the same page, you could say, that we were in the passing game as a unit all season. So, I thought there were a lot of positives. After the game, Liam and I talked; I saw him in the line doing TSA screening, and we were sitting there waiting. He was like, 'Man, I thought you played good. I know we had some turnovers, you had a throw or two you’d want back, but I thought you played well.' And I told him I felt the same way.

After that game, the Jaguars were practically unstoppable. They won their remaining six games and won the AFC South division title , but they ran into Josh Allen's Buffalo Bills in the first round of the playoffs.

Still, Lawrence showed immense growth late in the season. Following that Cardinals game, Lawrence threw 15 touchdowns and just one interceptions across his final six games . He also added four rushing touchdowns .

While his performance against the Bills against the playoffs saw him throw two interceptions, he still moved the ball enough to score three touchdowns. At 26 years old and in his second season alongside Coen, "T-Law" could be set for a true breakout in 2026 .

articles.title: Jaguars don’t need Travis Hunter at receiver, and that’s good news for their defense
articles.standfirst: Jacksonville expects the former Heisman Trophy winner to have a great sophomore season
articles.summary: Jacksonville expects the former Heisman Trophy winner to have a great sophomore season
articles.body:
When the Jacksonville Jaguars selected Travis Hunter with the No. 2 overall pick, they did so with a vision unlike anything the NFL has seen in decades. The former Heisman Trophy winner arrived in Jacksonville carrying the expectation that he could contribute on both sides of the ball, a rare challenge in a league that has become increasingly specialized.

A season-ending knee injury interrupted Hunter’s rookie campaign before that experiment could fully develop, but the Jaguars remain committed to making him a true two-way player. The difference entering 2026 is that Jacksonville appears ready to place a greater emphasis on Hunter’s defensive responsibilities.

General manager James Gladstone made that clear during an offseason appearance on The Rich Eisen Show, revealing that Hunter’s cornerback workload is expected to increase significantly compared to his rookie season. The shift reflects both Travis' unique skill set and the Jaguars’ evolving roster construction.

Jacksonville's receiving corps took a major step forward

During his abbreviated rookie season, Hunter spent the majority of his snaps on offense. According to Next Gen Stats, 305 of his 459 offensive and defensive snaps came at wide receiver. He functioned primarily as Jacksonville’s third or fourth receiving option , finishing with 28 receptions for 298 yards and one touchdown across seven games.

His most memorable performance came shortly before his injury. In a loss to the Los Angeles Rams in London, Hunter showcased the explosive talent that made him one of the most coveted prospects in recent memory. He hauled in eight passes for 101 yards on 14 targets and scored his first NFL touchdown , offering a glimpse of what he could become as an offensive weapon.

Yet despite those flashes, Jacksonville’s current roster gives the coaching staff the luxury of not relying heavily on Travis as a receiver. The Jaguars’ receiving corps took a major step forward while Hunter was sidelined. Veteran acquisition Jakobi Meyers quickly developed chemistry with quarterback Trevor Lawrence, Parker Washington emerged as a legitimate playmaker, and Brian Thomas Jr. rediscovered the downfield explosiveness that made him one of the league’s most dangerous young receivers.

The Jaguars’ defensive needs also point in that direction

With those three options firmly established, Jacksonville does not need Hunter to carry a significant offensive workload every week. Instead, the Jaguars can deploy him strategically, allowing him to focus on the side of the ball where he may ultimately have the highest ceiling.

Even before he entered the NFL , many evaluators believed Hunter’s future might be brightest at cornerback. His elite instincts, ball-tracking ability, and natural feel for reading quarterbacks have long made him one of football’s most gifted defensive prospects. The Jaguars’ defensive needs also point in that direction.

After significant changes in the secondary, Jacksonville entered the season with an opening opposite Montaric “Buster” Brown , who earned a lucrative contract extension following a breakout campaign. Defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile has also adjusted the scheme, moving toward more match-coverages and man principles rather than relying heavily on traditional zone concepts.

The new approach aligns perfectly with Hunter’s strengths. Few defensive backs possess his combination of athleticism, recovery speed, and ball skills. Placing him at left cornerback allows Jacksonville to maximize those traits while putting him in position to challenge opposing quarterbacks more frequently.
